validity.researcher_notes: Sheet: segment 'Phase I', LengthKnown=44.00 km, StartYear1=2019. Cross-checked against the sheet's own cited leads (wiki_citations.json) plus one open-web source. NS Energy Business project database (independent industry pipeline-project profile, cited by the wiki page itself) states explicitly: 'The Kochi-Koottanad-Bangalore-Mangalore pipeline project was split into two development phases with phase one involving a 41km-long pipeline section between Kochi and Koottanad in Kerala... The phase one section of the pipeline was successfully completed and commissioned in August 2013.' Indian Express (2021-01-11, also cited on the wiki page) independently corroborates the length: 'In the first phase, a 44-km line was laid in Kochi, linking the terminal with local industrial users, including Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited.' Both sources describe the SAME 41-44 km first-phase segment (rounding difference only) and both place it years before 2019 (approved June 2009, commissioned Aug 2013). The 2019 date instead matches NS Energy's description of Phase II's Kochi-Mangalore sub-segment ('the 440km pipeline stretch between Kochi and Mangalore via Koottanad which was successfully completed and commissioned in June 2019') -- a different, much longer stretch that is NOT captured by this 44 km row. So the sheet has paired the correct Phase-I length with the wrong phase's commissioning year. Two independent sources agree on both the 44 km figure (confirming LengthKnown) and on 2013 as Phase I's actual completion year (contradicting StartYear1=2019) -> high tier on the length confirmation, high tier on the date correction.

validity.researcher_notes: worklist.json flags this Location unit irregular=true because StartLocation and EndLocation are both 'Kochi' -- i.e. a 44 km pipeline with no distinct endpoint recorded. NS Energy Business explicitly names the Phase I terminus: 'phase one involving a 41km-long pipeline section between Kochi and Koottanad in Kerala' -- and 'Koottanad' is literally the second word of the pipeline's own name (Kochi-Koottanad-Bangalore-Mangalore), so the project's own naming convention corroborates the NS Energy statement rather than conflicting with it. Indian Express does not name the far end explicitly (it describes Phase I in terms of local industrial offtake -- BPCL etc. -- within Kochi), which is compatible with a Kochi-to-Koottanad trunk that taps industrial users near the Kochi end; it is not independent corroboration of 'Koottanad' as the endpoint, so I am calling this medium tier (one explicit named-endpoint source, corroborated by the pipeline's own name, not by a second independent narrative source).

validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: real, well-documented, currently-operating GAIL asset -- extensive independent press coverage across a decade (Mint 2012 regulatory approval, Economic Times 2016 extension / 2020 completion, The Hindu 2017 and The News Minute 2017 on right-of-way protests, Indian Express 2021, NS Energy project database), none of it GEM-derived. Not a hallucination. CLASSIFICATION: PipelineType=transmission is correct -- PNGRB's own May-2026 line-wise register (data-bank/20260531-NGPL-MIS-Report.pdf, printed p.2, 'PARTIALLY COMMISSIONED COMMON CARRIER PIPELINE' table, row 5) lists 'Kochi-Koottanad-Bangalore-Mangalore' as a common-carrier (transmission-class) authorized pipeline, entity GAIL, authorisation date 31.05.2012, authorised length 1,104 km, authorised/design capacity 16.0 MMSCMD -- exactly matching the Capacity value on BOTH of GEM's split rows for this project (P0934=16.00 and, per the fresh GGIT gas CSV, P2746 'construction' also =16.00). This is the known GEM convention (documented for this country: India CapacityBcm/y is derived from PNGRB's authorised, project-level MMSCMD and is duplicated across split operating/construction rows), not an error -- so Capacity=16.00 stands even though NS Energy separately gives Phase I's own narrower design throughput as 6 Mcm/d; I am not recommending a change. DUPLICATE check against the 35-row operating roster: no match -- none of the other 34 pipelines describe this route. There IS a companion row for the same project, P2746 ('construction', 1060 km, Koottanad->Mangalore, StartYear1=2022), and 44+1060=1104 km ties out exactly to PNGRB's current authorised total -- this is the documented granularity pattern (one authorised asset split into an operating row + a construction row), not a duplicate. CAVEAT for the record (not actioned here, outside P0934's 'Phase I' scope): PNGRB's CURRENT report shows the system-wide OPERATING length at 675 km and under-construction at 429 km (of 1,104 km authorised), whereas GEM's split is booked as 44 km operating / 1,060 km construction. The gap (roughly 630 km) most plausibly reflects the ~440-444 km Kochi-Mangalore leg that NS Energy/Indian Express both say was commissioned/opened in June 2019/Jan 2021 and is therefore now operating, but which GEM has not captured as its own operating row -- it appears to still be counted inside P2746's 1,060 km 'construction' figure. That is a P2746-side question (which row this shard does not own) and a possible new-segment/discovery question, not a P0934 defect, since P0934 is specifically scoped and named 'Phase I' (the original 41-44 km Kochi-Koottanad stretch) and its own length/capacity check out. Flagging for Update/Discovery follow-up on P2746 rather than changing anything here. summary: P0934 (Kochi-Koottanad-Bangalore-Mangalore, Phase I, 44 km) is a real, well-corroborated operating GAIL asset, correctly split from companion row P2746 (not a duplicate) and correctly classified/owned/fueled -- but StartYear1=2019 is wrong (should be 2013; 2019 belongs to a different, later-built leg of the same project) and EndLocation wrongly repeats 'Kochi' instead of the sourced terminus 'Koottanad'; both are staged as concerns, no fills added (no genuinely-blank fields could be safely sourced).
